finding: CPU physical projection rebuilt a batch descriptor and column directory for identity mappings on every scanner batch. On the many-page fixture, projection and ownership work were substantial sampled costs.
fix: Recognize identity mappings in the generic CPU project operator: implicit/all-column selections, wildcard selections with only existing names, and explicit unchanged column order, with no computed projection entries.
Reuse the physical input batch without new descriptor allocation; preserve backend selection, assessment, execution metrics and budget checks.
Keep the standalone vectorProjectBatch directory-copy contract; subsets, reordering, aliases and errors use the existing projector.

conformance.history: First identity-projection run still timed out on the page-count fixture. After clean timing comparisons, the complete unchanged suite passed; no timeout or assertion adjustment.

benchmark.caveat: Initial comparison overlapped type checking early in the run. The clean repeat ran without other agent tests/checks and confirms the improvement. Alternating fresh processes substitute only the prior physical executor with current dependencies; not a full historical build or cloud measurement.

boundaries: Input vectors remain borrowed by the physical result; existing execution scopes/owners retain their backing.
Physical fragment construction/fingerprinting and planning still occur for each batch; this introduces no growing cache.
A passing full conformance run and lower standalone medians do not guarantee a wall-clock bound under arbitrary host load. No timeout or assertions were weakened.
